newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Family seeks news of Briton kidnapped in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Family seeks news of Briton kidnapped in Cambodia.

text.p: The family of a British explosives expert kidnapped in Cambodia in March appealed for information on his whereabouts in a Monday newspaper.
Christopher Howes, 36, of the British-based Mines Advisory Group (MAG), and his interpreter, Houn Hourth, were abducted by armed men in the northwestern province of Siem Reap on March 26.
Howes' parents, in a letter published in the Cambodia Daily, said the family was suffering "great distress" at the lack of information on his fate.
His mother, Betty, "particularly appeals to other mothers and indeed all women who may be able to help", the letter said.
The MAG had received often conflicting reports on the fate of the two men, MAG programme director Archie McCarron said on Monday.

Howes had only been working a few months as a mine clearance supervisor for MAG, an agency helping to clear some four to six million mines scattered around the country in more than two decades of war between the government and rebel Khmer Rouge.

A Bangkok Post article in late August cited an unnamed officer of the Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement as saying that Howes had been executed in the Khmer Rouge stronghold of Anlong Veng. It said Houn Hourth died of malaria in July.
Khmer Rouge radio later denied that the guerrilla group had killed Howes.
The Maoist Khmer Rouge signed a UN-brokered peace accord in 1991 but later reneged on the pact and has been fighting the coalition government that emerged from general elections in 1993.
The guerrillas have abducted several foreigners in the past, releasing only a handful and killing at least seven.
Khmer Rouge commanders in northwest Cambodia split from hardliners last month and are talking peace with the government.
